why: Intro to Git and GitHub plan (docs/ui-next/catalog/plans/intro-git.json), 'Push the cookbook to GitHub' (passes: origin points at GitHub and origin/main matches the local main branch). The learner used the GitHub CLI instead: `gh repo create cookbook --public --source=. --remote=origin --push` made the repository, added origin and pushed. gh pushes HEAD, so git's line reads '* [new branch] HEAD -> main' (not 'main -> main'), then "branch 'main' set up to track 'origin/main'". `git remote -v` shows origin at github.com and `git status` says up to date with 'origin/main'. Done.

step.title: Push the cookbook to GitHub
step.instructions: Make an empty repository named cookbook on GitHub, add it as origin with git remote add origin git@github.com:<you>/cookbook.git, then git push -u origin main. Run git remote -v to check.
